PART A
Question #1
```{r}
#"A" adds up the numbers in each row of the matrix and returns one total for every row, while "B" #does the same for each column. "C" returns a list, because `lapply` always returns its results in #list form. "D" squares each number and returns the answers as a simple vector, and "E" counts the #letters in each word and labels each count with the word it belongs to. "F" multiplies the two sets #of numbers together, matching them up position by position, and "G" adds up the numbers within each #group and returns one total for every group.
```
Question #2
```{r}
scores <- matrix(c(70, 85, 90,
                   60, 75, 80,
                   88, 92, 79),
                 nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE,
                 dimnames = list(c('Ana', 'Ben', 'Cara'), c('Math', 'Sci', 'Eng')))
 
temps <- list(Mon = c(30, 32, 31), Tue = c(29, 33), Wed = c(31, 34, 35, 30))
apply(scores, 1, mean)
apply(scores, 2, max)
apply(scores, 1, function(row) names(which.max(row)))


lapply(temps, mean)
sapply(temps, length)
vapply(temps, range, numeric(2))

#The range result is a matrix because range() returns two values per day. vapply stacks them as #columns, one per day. A single value per day would give a vector.
```

Question #3
```{r}
principal <- c(1000, 2000)
rate      <- c(0.05, 0.04)
years     <- c(2, 3)

mapply(function(p, r, n) p * (1 + r)^n, principal, rate, years)
mapply(function(p, n, r) p * (1 + r)^n,
       p = principal, n = years,
       MoreArgs = list(r = 0.045))
```
Question #4
```{r}
tapply(iris$Sepal.Length, iris$Species, mean)
table(mtcars$cyl, mtcars$am)
tapply(mtcars$mpg, mtcars$cyl, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
```

PART B
Question #5
```{r}
sapply(list(a = 1:3, b = 4:6), mean)
# Use mean, not mean(). Parentheses run the function right away, but sapply only needs its name.

apply(matrix(1:6, nrow = 3), 2, mean)
# 1 means rows and 2 means columns. Use 2 to get one mean per column.

df <- data.frame(n = c(1, 2), s = c('a', 'b'))
sapply(df, class)
# apply turns everything into text, but sapply checks each column on its own.
```

Question #6
```{r}
#1.lapply() always returns a list. sapply() does the same job but simplifies the result into a vector or matrix when it can. I would use vapply() when I want a safe, predictable result. With it, I state the type of each result in advance, and R gives an error if something doesn't match.

#2 tapply(x, g, mean) does it in one call. It returns one mean per group as a named array, not a list.
```
